title: Candidate, electoral right defined
old_text: Defined 'candidate' as a person nominated at any election, and 'electoral right' as the right to stand, withdraw, vote or refrain from voting.
new_text: Defines 'candidate' as a person who has been nominated as a candidate at any election, and 'electoral right' as the right to stand, or not to stand as, or to withdraw from being, a candidate, or to vote or refrain from voting at an election.
explanation: Provides statutory definitions for candidate and electoral right governing all election-related penal offences. Renumbered from IPC Section 171A.

title: Bribery
old_text: Defined bribery as giving gratification to induce the exercise of an electoral right or accepting such gratification, with an exception for public policy declarations.
new_text: Defines the offence of electoral bribery (giving gratification to induce voting behavior or accepting reward), preserving the carve-out for declarations of public policy or promises of public action.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 171E.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 173.
explanation: Prohibits monetary or material inducements aimed at swaying voter franchise or candidate nominations. Renumbered from IPC Section 171B.

title: Undue influence at elections
old_text: Defined undue influence as voluntarily interfering or attempting to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right, including threats of injury or spiritual displeasure.
new_text: Defines undue influence as voluntarily interfering or attempting to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right, including threats of injury or divine/spiritual displeasure.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 171F.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 174.
explanation: Guarantees free voter choice by criminalizing voter coercion, intimidation, social boycotts, or invoking divine displeasure. Renumbered from IPC Section 171C.

title: Personation at elections
old_text: Defined personation as applying for a voting paper or voting in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or applying to vote more than once.
new_text: Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper or votes in the name of any other person, whether living, dead, or fictitious, or having voted once applies again to vote, commits personation.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under IPC Section 171F.
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed under BNS Section 174.
explanation: Criminalizes bogus voting, impersonating deceased or absent voters, and multiple voting. Renumbered from IPC Section 171D.

title: Punishment for bribery
old_text: Punished electoral bribery with imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both; bribery by treating punished with fine only.
new_text: Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both; bribery by treating is punished with fine only.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both; treating: fine only (IPC Section 171E).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one year, or with fine, or with both; treating: fine only (BNS Section 173).
explanation: Prescribes sentencing for electoral bribery, differentiating direct bribery from petty bribery by treating (hospitality/food). Renumbered from IPC Section 171E.

title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election
old_text: Punished undue influence or personation at an election with imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever commits the offence of undue influence or personation at an election shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both (IPC Section 171F).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one year, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 174).
explanation: Punishes electoral intimidation and fraudulent voter impersonation with up to one year imprisonment or fine. Renumbered from IPC Section 171F.

title: False statement in connection with an election
old_text: Penalized publishing false statements of fact regarding the personal character or conduct of a candidate with fine.
new_text: Whoever, with intent to affect the result of an election, makes or publishes any statement purporting to be a statement of fact which is false regarding the personal character or conduct of any candidate, shall be punished with fine.
explanation: Penalizes malicious character assassination, smears, and fabricated factual assertions directed against candidates to manipulate election outcomes. Renumbered from IPC Section 171G.

title: Illegal payments in connection with an election
old_text: Penalized incurring unauthorized election expenses without written candidate authority with fine up to ₹500.
new_text: Whoever, without general or special authority in writing of a candidate, incurs or authorizes expenses on public meetings, advertisements, or circulars for promoting the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
punishment_new: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees (BNS Section 176).
explanation: Enforces election spending transparency by penalizing unauthorized third-party political financing, increasing the maximum fine tenfold from ₹500 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 171H.

title: Failure to keep election accounts
old_text: Penalized failing to keep accounts of election expenses as legally required with fine up to ₹500.
new_text: Whoever, being required by any law for the time being in force to keep accounts of expenses incurred at or in connection with an election, fails to keep such accounts, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
punishment_new: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees (BNS Section 177).
explanation: Penalizes candidates and agents who fail to maintain statutory campaign accounting logs, raising the maximum fine from ₹500 to ₹5,000. Renumbered from IPC Section 171I.
